Q: Are system calls actually APIs? A:

API stands for Application Programming Interface, i.e. facilities intended to be used by application programmers. Depending on a particular OS, syscalls might be APIs - if they are documented as such. They are often not, though.

Linux is a bad example for looking at this, as its libc functions are mostly 1:1 mappings to syscalls (altough not all of them, e.g. gettimeofday is an example of API function which is usually not going through syscall at all). Windows is a better example: its syscalls are opaque, undocumented and very different from user-facing Win32 API.

Q: Pygame - Creating a "Enemy" class, and then importing it into game A:

import pygame

from player import Player

from enemies import EnemyManager

from guns import GunManager

from powerups import PowerUpManager

pygame.init()

WIDTH, HEIGHT = 1000, 650

screen = pygame.display.set_mode((WIDTH, HEIGHT))

pygame.display.set_caption("ULTIMATE GUN GAME")

clock = pygame.time.Clock()

font = pygame.font.SysFont(None, 30)

player = Player(WIDTH//2, HEIGHT//2)

guns = GunManager()

enemies = EnemyManager()

powerups = PowerUpManager()

running = True

while running:

clock.tick(60)

screen.fill((20,20,20))

for event in pygame.event.get():

    if event.type == pygame.QUIT:

        running = False

    if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:

        if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:

            running = False

        if event.unicode.isdigit():

            guns.switch(int(event.unicode))

player.update()

bullets = guns.update(player)

enemies.update(player, bullets)

powerups.update(player)

player.draw(screen)

guns.draw(screen)

enemies.draw(screen)

powerups.draw(screen)

ui = font.render(f"HP:{player.hp}  Gun:{guns.current_name()}  Score:{enemies.score}", True, (255,255,255))

screen.blit(ui, (10,10))

if player.hp \<= 0:

    screen.blit(font.render("GAME OVER", True, (255,0,0)), (450,300))

    pygame.display.flip()

    pygame.time.wait(2000)

    break

pygame.display.flip()

pygame.quit()

Q: Regarding using the API links in Springboot application A:

Depends on which environment

  • For local development you should use .env or application-secret.yml
  • In production use environment variables
  • On cloud use a Secrets Manager or Vault, or for Docker/Kubernetes inject secrets at runtime.
